title: GPX Maximum Speed Calculator: Fastest Segment
description: Find the fastest timestamped segment in a GPX track with the GPX Maximum Speed Calculator — distance over time, segment by segment. Free, local.
summary_sentence: For example, a segment covering 100 metres in 8 seconds runs at 12.5 metres per second — exactly 45.0 km/h — and the calculator hunts the whole file for the pair of points that beats it.
quick_answer: The GPX Maximum Speed Calculator scans a GPX track segment by segment — distance divided by elapsed time between consecutive timestamped points — and reports the fastest one. Load the file locally and read your top speed — with the caveat that one noisy point can invent a legend.

for the plausible frame around the peak.
A maximum of 300 km/h on a bicycle is not fitness, it is a bad fix. The fastest segment's location in the file is where the corruption lives.
Fleet and courier GPX logs answer 'how fast did it actually go?' from the recording, segment by segment.
Before a dataset of tracks feeds any analysis, maximum-speed outliers flag the files that need cleaning.
Consecutive points 100 m apart with stamps 8 seconds apart: 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 m/s, × 3.6 = 45.0 km/h. Every top-speed figure is this division applied to the file's best pair — no pair, no speed.

A single fix jumping 50 metres sideways in a 1-second interval reads as 180 km/h. In a tunnel exit or a city canyon, that phantom tops the chart — which is why this page pairs the result with the spike warning rather than a trophy.

popular_table.note: Averaging speed over longer windows tames noise; the maximum over single segments amplifies it. Read the number with its recording conditions, as this table does.

faq: Consecutive trackpoints carrying both coordinates and timestamps, within each track segment — segments never leap across the gaps where recording paused.
What if the file has no timestamps?
No time, no speed: positions alone cannot make a rate. The Timestamp Span tool shows what time data a file actually holds.
Yes — km/h and mph both, per this site's convention. Downhill sports quote both dialects depending on continent.
Platforms smooth; this calculator reports the file's own fastest segment so you can see what smoothing would be hiding. Knowing the raw peak is the point of the page.
Downhill versus flat — does slope matter?
The speed is horizontal ground speed from coordinates and time. Slope is real effort the number ignores — the elevation tools carry the vertical story.
A route's rtept stamps are usually the planner's fiction; speeds from them describe the plan, not a journey. Recorded tracks are the evidence.
